title.narrative: Improving the standards compliance through increased national capacities for residue monitoring

description.narrative:
The overall objective of this Action is to enhance national consumer safety and access to safe, healthy and nutritious food and to improve trade opportunities and create a conducive business environment for SMEs, thus contributing to resilient, sustainable, and inclusive economic development as well as paving the way to a fully-fledged Green Deal for the Republic of Moldova.

The specific objective of the Action is to increase national capacities for residue monitoring in animal feed and products of animal origin (pesticides, veterinary medicine, contaminants and prohibited substances).

The Action will pursue three technical Outcomes, thus responding to the limited capacity for residues monitoring and the main compliance challenges identified in the Republic of Moldova:

Outcome 1: Improved practices of competent authorities (ANSA and MAFI) through good governance and revamped legal and regulatory framework.

Institutional strengthening of the ANSA and MAFI through capacity building, use of best practices, skills development, and implementation of management systems.

Outcome 2: Improved practices of national reference laboratories through expanded testing capacities, demonstrating proof of compliance.

Strengthening the National reference laboratories through capacity building, use of best practices, skills development, procurement of minor laboratory equipment and implementation of management systems, accreditation and validation of methods to ensure quality and international recognition of their services with a focus on pesticide and veterinary drug residues.

Outcome 3: SMEs and FBOs awareness and application of best practises in compliance with standards and technical regulations in the value chains of meat, poultry and milk products are enhanced.

Improving compliance capacity and awareness through specialised training and capacity building for SMEs and FBOs

Increased compliance of producers and agri-food products with a maximum permissible limit of pesticides and veterinary drugs is understood as an intermediate impact outcome.

description.narrative: SMEs and FBOs in the value chains of meat, poultry and milk products will be strengthened to have the capacity to produce higher and improved quality products. To achieve this, technical training programmes and direct coaching will be provided at the producers level to reduce the use of toxic substances and veterinary drugs and medicines. Part of the interventions will also include creating awareness of legal requirements and standards as well as knowledge of the available best practices that can be implemented by SMEs, FBOs, veterinary pharmacies and veterinarians with strong and proactive involvement of the local support institutions.Also, as the laboratories mandate does not cover the sampling process, the accuracy of the quality of samples collected and submitted to the laboratories is difficult to control, which often leads to inaccurate testing results. Under the interventions, special attention will therefore be paid to strengthening the capacities of producers and FBOs to improve the sampling process for selfcontrols.Furthermore, the project will also aim to support SMEs and FBOs in the selected value chains to overcome barriers to growth by increasing their collective efficiency to jointly benefit from the improved capacity of residue monitoring. The project will explore opportunities for the application of the cluster development approach by supporting the formulation of collective action plans, establishing first activities and strengthening interfirm cooperation.rs and achieving capital preservation for Class B Limited Partners via medium to longterm capital appreciation.

description.narrative: SMEs and FBOs in the value chains of meat, poultry and milk products will be strengthened to have the capacity to produce higher and improved quality products. To achieve this, technical training programmes and direct coaching will be provided at the producers level to reduce the use of toxic substances and veterinary drugs and medicines. Part of the interventions will also include creating awareness of legal requirements and standards as well as knowledge of the available best practices that can be implemented by SMEs, FBOs, veterinary pharmacies and veterinarians with strong and proactive involvement of the local support institutions.Also, as the laboratories mandate does not cover the sampling process, the accuracy of the quality of samples collected and submitted to the laboratories is difficult to control, which often leads to inaccurate testing results. Under the interventions, special attention will therefore be paid to strengthening the capacities of producers and FBOs to improve the sampling process for selfcontrols.The project will also aim to support SMEs and FBOs in the selected value chains to overcome barriers to growth by increasing their collective efficiency to jointly benefit from the improved capacity of residue monitoring. The project will explore opportunities for the application of the cluster development approach by supporting the formulation of collective action plans, establishing first activities and strengthening interfirm cooperation.Furthermore, the project will raise quality awareness by promoting a culture of quality, including European standards and testing requirements, for support institutions and producers in the selected value chains and clusters. As quality does not only refer to products but extends to all areas of production, distribution and management, the project will target the consumers as awarenessraising activities will help to introduce a consumption pattern, which prioritizes purchasing and consumption of quality products.
